name: the backdrop stays on above the dock (wide window)
why: Reported 2026-11-16: a header block pushed out of the window by its parent's end is ABOVE its dock; with <= the backdrop stayed on as a white band the page scrolled behind.
grep: wide window: the backdrop is there

name: the backdrop stays on above the dock (phone)
why: The same guard at the phone's own width, where it was reported.
grep: phone: the toolbar h1 docks at the very top

name: the navbar height counts whether or not the navbar can be fixed
why: Up to 992 px the site keeps its navbar in the flow (position: relative !important); reserving its 80 px left a gap above the docked h1 that the page showed through.
grep: narrow window: the site leaves its navbar in the flow

name: the navbar height counts whether or not the navbar can be fixed (phone)
why: The same guard at the phone's own width.
grep: phone: the toolbar h1 docks at the very top

name: the trial position: fixed stays on the navbar
why: The measurement sets position: fixed inline for one read; left there, the navbar would be fixed at the top of an unscrolled page.
grep: the list h2 docks under the site's navbar

name: no re-measure of the navbar on a window resize
why: Known overlap: with the sticky filter bars on, _vsbBaseOffset() calls _slNavbarOffset() on every refresh, and a resize schedules one. The listener of _slPrepareLivePage() only matters with the bars switched off (the thead rule reads the variable), which no spec resizes.
grep: the list h2 docks under the site's navbar

name: the toolbar h1 is never moved out of .project-detail
why: Reported 2026-11-16 (debug/SL-sticky-area-sticky-then-moved-IP.mp4): where the site closes .project-detail right after the category walls, the h1 docked only until .project-detail ended, then scrolled away.
grep: collection-intro \(initial page\): the header block stays docked

name: the toolbar h1 is never moved out of .project-detail (after the press)
why: The same at the FRP: the table sits in a later container than .project-detail.
grep: memorabilia \(after the press\): the header block stays docked

name: the toolbar h1 is never moved out of .project-detail (phone)
why: The same at the phone's own width.
grep: phone: the toolbar h1 docks at the very top

name: the header wrapper gets no side padding
why: On memorabilia the h1 leaves the floated .col-sm-12 and its 15 px gutter; without the padding it moves 15 px to the left.
grep: memorabilia: the h1 moved out of .project-detail keeps its place

name: the h1 is wrapped even where the list is inside .project-detail
why: Pages whose data is inside .project-detail work as they are and must stay byte-identical: no wrapper.
grep: a list inside .project-detail: the h1 is left where it is

name: no second placement before the bars measure after a render
why: Known overlap: every SL fixture's table lands in the same container as its list, so the placement at init already holds after the press (scripts/probe-sl-sticky-head.probe.js). The call in initStickyFilterBars() is for a table that lands elsewhere, which no fixture has.
grep: \(after the press\): the header block stays docked

name: the status line is not taken into the wrapper
why: Known overlap: at init the status line does not exist yet, and is inserted after the h1, so inside the wrapper. Taking it along matters only for a move after init, which no fixture has (see the entry above).
grep: the header block stays docked past the end of .project-detail

name: no viewport fit after a render
why: Reported 2026-11-16/17 (debug/SL-firefox-FRP-non-sticky.*): with the site's width=device-width, initial-scale=1 a mobile browser widens the layout viewport to the table, and nothing sticky reaches the visible top.
grep: phone, after the press: the layout viewport stays the screen

name: the viewport tag never gets minimum-scale=1
why: minimum-scale=1 is what keeps the layout viewport at the screen's width (checked by vzell in Firefox's responsive mode, 2026-11-17).
grep: phone, after the press: the layout viewport stays the screen

name: the site's own viewport tag is never put back
why: Once the table fits the window again (a rotation, a tablet), zooming out is the site's to allow.
grep: phone, after the press: the layout viewport stays the screen

name: no viewport fit on resize
why: The restore case widens the window without a render, so only the resize listener runs the fit again; after a rotation the tag would stay as it was.
grep: phone, after the press: the layout viewport stays the screen
